claims.text: Conventional casting of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi yields a coarse-grained, primarily FCC solid-solution structure.
Cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has a low dislocation density.
The coarse-grained, low-dislocation-density state causes the relatively low hardness and strength of cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The primarily FCC matrix contributes to the favorable plasticity of cast CoCrFeNiTi.
HEBM followed by SPS produces a nonequilibrium nanocrystalline CoCrFeNiTi microstructure.
HEBM followed by SPS produces an approximately 83% FCC and 17% BCC phase mixture in CoCrFeNiTi.
The stated HEBM/SPS treatment reduces the crystal grain size to below approximately 48 nm.
The stated HEBM/SPS treatment produces severe lattice strain.
Nanocrystalline grain refinement increases hardness and compressive strength through Hall–Petch grain-boundary strengthening.
HEBM/SPS increases dislocation density, which contributes to increased hardness and strength.
The titanium-influenced minor BCC phase may provide an additional strengthening contribution.
Strengthening by HEBM/SPS is expected to reduce ductility relative to the cast alloy.
HEBM/SPS-processed equimolar CoCrFeNiTi should reach approximately 675 HV Vickers hardness.
HEBM/SPS-processed equimolar CoCrFeNiTi should reach approximately 1894 MPa compressive strength.
HEBM/SPS-processed samples should exhibit intergranular fracture features associated with high strength and limited ductility.
The conventional cast baseline has higher porosity than the HEBM/SPS-processed alloy.
The proposed strengthening applies at room temperature under compressive loading for milling durations up to about 6 hours and SPS temperatures up to 1000 °C.
Processing beyond the stated limits may cause grain coarsening or phase instability that negates the strengthening benefits.
